I am 62 years old and I have farmed these 13.1 mu in Quzhou for 40 years. I only went to primary school, but I know my land. My family has seven people and some of my children work in the county town, so I do most of the field work myself. I have a well, so I can irrigate when the weather turns dry.

This year I will do more or less what I did last year, because last year was not bad and change is risky. I have 7 mu for my wheat-maize rotation, 4 mu for cotton, and 2.1 mu for mungbean.

For wheat, I will plant Jimai 22 on 7 mu. That is the same improved variety my neighbor Old Wang used last year and his wheat looked good. In October I will rotary till the ground and put down half a bag — 50 jin — of compound fertilizer per mu as basal. Then in March, when the wheat turns green, I will spread another 40 jin of urea per mu. I will irrigate three times: once before winter, once at green-up, and once at heading. That costs money for electricity, but without water the yield drops. I will spray three times — herbicide once and insecticide twice — because the aphids and rust always come. I expect about 1000 jin per mu, same as last year.

For maize, I will sow Denghai 605 right after the wheat harvest in June. I do not till for maize — I no-till plant directly into the wheat stubble. This saves time and diesel. I put 50 jin of compound fertilizer in the row at sowing, and then side-dress with 50 jin of urea when the plants are knee-high. I will irrigate twice, once if June is dry and once in August when the ears fill. Three sprays total — herbicide at sowing and insecticide twice for the corn borer. I expect around 1050 jin per mu.

For cotton on my 4 mu, I will use variety 99-1. I have used it for years. I rotary till in April and put down 60 jin of compound per mu as basal, then 30 jin of urea when the plants flower. Cotton drinks less water than corn, so two irrigations is enough, but the bugs are terrible. I will spray 12 times — bollworm, aphids, whitefly, they never stop. I hire the spraying machine from the village. I hope for 260 jin of seed cotton per mu.

For mungbean on 2.1 mu, I plant traditional seed in June. Mungbean does not need much nitrogen — the roots make their own — but I spread 20 jin of compound per mu to help them start. Two irrigations and three sprays. I expect about 100 jin per mu. My wife likes mungbean for porridge in summer, and the leftover I can sell in the market.

Every jin of fertilizer is real money. A bag of urea is over 100 yuan now. But I would rather put a bit too much than too little. If I lose the crop, my whole year is ruined. I watch what my neighbors do. If Old Wang puts 50 jin of urea on his corn, I do the same. That is how I decide.

I follow last year's practices because they worked: Jimai 22 wheat with rotary tillage, Denghai 605 maize with no-tillage, 99-1 cotton, and traditional mungbean.
